question.text: Consider $\mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{k}_{1}} \mathrm{~B}$ and $\mathrm{C} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{k}_{2}} \mathrm{D}$ are two reactions. If the rate constant $\left(\mathrm{k}_{1}\right)$ of the $\mathrm{A} \longrightarrow \mathrm{B}$ reaction can be expressed by the following equation $\log _{10} \mathrm{k}=14.34-\frac{1.5 \times 10^{4}}{\mathrm{~T} / \mathrm{K}}$ and activation energy of $C \longrightarrow D$ reaction $\left(E a_{2}\right)$ is $\frac{1}{5}$ th of the $A \longrightarrow B$ reaction $\left(E a_{1}\right)$, then the value of $\left(E a_{2}\right)$ is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer)
